Bloom Energy, 13 Apr 2026 (BusinessWire 14 Apr): under a master services agreement Oracle intends to procure up to 2.8 gigawatts of Bloom's fuel cell systems; an initial 1.2 GW is contracted, with deployment underway and continuing into next year.

Bloom Energy Q1 2026 results, 28 Apr 2026 (8-K exhibit 99.1): revenue $751.1 million, up 130.4% from $326.0 million; product revenue $653.3 million, up 208.4%; GAAP operating income $72.2 million; full-year 2026 revenue guidance raised to $3.4-3.8 billion, growth midpoint lifted from ~60% to ~80%.

8 Jan 2026 (AEP disclosure, reported by Investing.com, TradingView, Fuel Cells Works): AEP's unregulated subsidiary exercised its option for a further 900 MW of Bloom solid-oxide fuel cells, a $2.65 billion agreement supporting a planned 900 MW facility in Wyoming backed by a 20-year offtake; the initial 100 MW was agreed in November 2025.

Bloom Energy / Brookfield: the strategic AI-infrastructure power partnership was first announced in October 2025 with a $5 billion framework to deploy Bloom fuel cells at AI data centres; on 30 Jun 2026 (after this brief's date) the framework was expanded fivefold to $25 billion.

Company profile: Bloom Energy Corporation, incorporated in 2001, headquartered in San Jose, California, NYSE: BE; designs, manufactures, sells and installs solid oxide fuel cell systems for on-site power generation; the Bloom Energy Server converts natural gas, biogas, hydrogen or a blend into electricity without combustion; customers span utilities, data centres, retail, healthcare, manufacturing.

Bloom Energy team page: Natalie Sunderland, Chief Marketing Officer, responsible for strengthening the company's market position, accelerating sales and growth, and building an iconic brand; two decades of marketing experience.
Bloom Energy 8-K (reported by StreetInsider): Aman Joshi appointed Executive Vice President, Chief Commercial Officer, effective 5 January 2024.

Bloom Energy, 26 Mar 2026: Simon Edwards appointed Chief Financial Officer effective 13 April 2026; he joined from AI-inference company Groq, where he was CFO and then CEO, having earlier been CFO of GE Digital, Conga and ServiceMax.

McLaren Racing, 26 Sep 2025: Groq announced as an Official Partner of the McLaren Formula 1 Team; Groq's LPU inference technology supports analysis, development and real-time insight; Groq branding on the cars from the 2025 Singapore Grand Prix.

Atlassian Williams F1 Team (Grove article) and local planning coverage (Wantage.com, 'Project Carrum'): a phased modernisation and expansion of the Grove campus adds new and larger factory, technology and testing facilities, new offices and staff facilities, with a scoping opinion lodged with Vale of White Horse District Council; 2026 is the team's 30th year at Grove. The Race: Dorilton has invested heavily since taking ownership in summer 2020 and brought in James Vowles from Mercedes.

TechTimes, 2 Jul 2026, on the Brookfield expansion: Oracle received its first Bloom system at an AI data-centre campus in 55 days, 35 days ahead of a 90-day target, before expanding to up to 2.8 GW (reported).

Toyota USA Newsroom, May 2026: Toyota's stationary fuel cell generators, built from Mirai fuel-cell system components, achieved ANSI/CSA FC 1 and FC 6 certification; Toyota positions them as lower-emission power for organisations.

General Motors, 10 Oct 2025: GM ends next-generation hydrogen fuel-cell development under its Hydrotec brand and winds down fuel-cell production for data centres and power generation at its joint venture with Honda.

Sponsor table: Williams — Atlassian (title), Gulf, Duracell, Stephens, Dorilton Ventures, SIA, Kraken, Komatsu, VAST, Keeper, Zoox, Betway, Airia, Brillio, NMC; no power-generation or energy-infrastructure partner. brief.deck: Bloom Energy, the San Jose fuel-cell maker now powering AI data centres for Oracle, American Electric Power and Brookfield, signed a master agreement for up to 2.8 GW of its systems with Oracle on 13 April 2026 and posted a record first quarter, lifting 2026 revenue guidance to $3.4-3.8B.
brief.the_case_p1: On 13 April Bloom and Oracle announced a master services agreement under which Oracle intends to procure up to 2.8 GW of Bloom fuel-cell systems, 1.2 GW contracted. Two weeks later Bloom reported first-quarter revenue of $751.1M, up 130.4%, and raised 2026 guidance to $3.4-3.8B; total backlog is about $20B. American Electric Power exercised a $2.65B option for 900 MW in January, and Brookfield committed $5B in October 2025 to finance Bloom-powered AI data centres. A niche fuel-cell company has become the power supplier of the AI build-out, and its brand has not caught up.
brief.the_case_p2: The grid sells energy at scale, but every energy partner on it is a fuel or lubricant brand: Aramco at Aston Martin, Petronas at Mercedes, Shell at Ferrari, Eni at Alpine, Mobil 1 and Esso at Red Bull. No team carries an on-site power generation partner, even as factories add simulators, data halls and wind-tunnel hours that local grids were never sized for. Bloom's product is that: baseload power delivered in months, not years.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  Bloom's 2026 guidance of $3.4-3.8B implies roughly 80% growth, raised on 28 April; the budget and the motive to be known beyond energy circles crest together. Austin (late October) and Las Vegas (November) are the US stages left in 2026, and teams close 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter.
brief.why_team_para: Williams is rebuilding Grove: a phased modernisation adds larger factory, technology and testing facilities. The roster carries Atlassian as title partner, Gulf in fuel, Duracell in consumer batteries, Komatsu, VAST and Keeper, but no power-generation or energy-infrastructure partner, so Official Power Partner is a clean category. Dorilton's investment since 2020 and a data-led revival under James Vowles give a US industrial brand a team that will use the product as well as show it.
brief.value_content: MODE A - operational. Grove's expansion adds simulator, data-hall and wind-tunnel load. Bloom Energy Servers generate power on site from natural gas, biogas or hydrogen without combustion; Oracle took its first system in 55 days, and that speed applies to a factory too. New buildings come online without waiting on a grid upgrade, with a lower-carbon footprint the team can report. In return: Official Power Partner status, rear-wing placement, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality for Bloom's customers.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Power Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, spanning the Grove build-out and the first Oracle gigawatts. Estimated $3-5M a year, part-deliverable as installed Energy Server capacity at Grove. Scope: rear-wing or engine-cover placement, naming of the factory's power plant, US-race hospitality, content on powering the campus.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Sridhar founded Bloom in 2001; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Natalie Sunderland, CMO, briefed to build an iconic brand; Aman Joshi, EVP and Chief Commercial Officer since January 2024; Simon Edwards, CFO since April 2026, previously CFO then CEO of McLaren partner Groq.
brief.opening_angle_intro: Lead with the Oracle gigawatts and the Grove build.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “KR, Oracle is putting up to 2.8 GW of your servers under its AI factories; Williams is rebuilding Grove and has no power partner. Your new CFO watched Groq take a McLaren seat. 25 minutes before Austin to see the numbers?”
score_cells: Oracle deal 13 Apr, guidance raised 28 Apr; Austin and Las Vegas in window.
Industrial B2B brand; CMO briefed to build an iconic brand.
AI power scramble is now; 2027 rosters close in Q4.
MODE A: on-site power for the Grove expansion.
risks: Gulf (fuel) and Duracell (batteries) could read a power partner as a category intrusion.
Define the category as stationary power generation; neither sells it.
Bloom's growth is US data centres; a UK factory installation needs a gas or hydrogen supply at Grove.
Lead with the US races and a Grove feasibility study; the installation follows the deal.
brief.bottom_line: Up to 2.8 GW with Oracle, a $2.65B AEP order, $5B from Brookfield and guidance of $3.4-3.8B put Bloom at peak brand-building capacity with a brand few outside energy know. Williams is expanding Grove and carries no power partner; the lane, the workstream and two US races line up before 2027 rosters close.

why_now.label: Trigger
why_now.text: On 13 April 2026 Bloom Energy and Oracle announced a master services agreement under which Oracle intends to procure up to 2.8 GW of Bloom's fuel-cell systems, with 1.2 GW already contracted and deployment running into 2027. It is the largest single commitment in Bloom's history and it was announced by the company itself.

why_now.label: Record quarter, guidance raised
why_now.text: On 28 April Bloom reported first-quarter revenue of $751.1M, up 130.4% on the year, and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $3.4-3.8B, roughly 80% growth at the midpoint. On the call the company put total backlog at about $20B, more than half of the data-centre portion from hyperscalers, neoclouds and colocation providers other than Oracle.

why_now.label: The order book behind it
why_now.text: American Electric Power exercised a $2.65B option for 900 MW of Bloom fuel cells on 8 January 2026 for a Wyoming data-centre campus, and Brookfield committed $5B in October 2025 to finance Bloom-powered AI data centres. A company selling power to the AI build-out in gigawatts is buying brand for the first time at scale; its CMO's stated brief is to build an iconic brand.

why_now.label: Calendar window
why_now.text: The US GP in Austin (late October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two US rounds left in 2026, and teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed before Austin can be announced in the US, where Bloom's customers sit, and activated in full for 2027.

why_team.label: The open lane
why_team.text: Williams carries Atlassian as title partner, Gulf in fuel, Duracell in consumer batteries, Komatsu in industrial equipment, VAST, Keeper, Airia and Brillio in technology. No power-generation or energy-infrastructure partner: Official Power Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price, without a title-level cheque.

why_team.label: A factory that needs power
why_team.text: Williams is in a phased modernisation of the Grove campus, adding new and larger factory, technology and testing facilities, offices and staff buildings, with a scoping opinion lodged with the district council. New buildings mean new load; on-site generation is a workstream the team would actually commission, not a logo.

why_team.label: Ownership and audience
why_team.text: Dorilton has invested heavily since taking ownership in 2020 and brought in James Vowles to run a data-led revival. A US-owned British team gives a San Jose industrial brand a home story on both sides of the Atlantic, and the Austin and Las Vegas suites put Bloom in front of the hyperscaler, utility and capital-markets guests it sells to.

why_team.label: Category discipline
why_team.text: Gulf and Duracell are energy-adjacent, so the category must be defined as stationary power generation from the first conversation; neither brand sells it. Aggreko supplies temporary power to the championship, not to a team, and does not block a team-level power partner.

value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)
value.text: Bloom Energy Servers convert natural gas, biogas or hydrogen into electricity on site without combustion. For Grove that means resilient baseload for the simulator, data hall and wind-tunnel programme as the campus grows, delivered on Bloom's data-centre timescales (Oracle took its first system in 55 days) rather than a grid-upgrade timescale, with a lower-carbon footprint the team can report.

value.label: Commercial lift for the team
value.text: Bloom sells to CIOs, utility executives and infrastructure investors. Its guest list at Austin and Las Vegas is the audience Williams' B2B partners want in the suite, and a partner with a $3.4-3.8B revenue base is a credible multi-year counterparty.

value.label: Content and ecosystem
value.text: A factory-power story the team can tell on camera: how a Formula 1 campus is powered, what the new buildings draw, and how fuel cells fit a lower-carbon plan. For Bloom, a reference installation outside the data-centre world, and engineering content with a team known for data.

value.label: What the team gives back
value.text: Official Power Partner designation, rear-wing or engine-cover placement, naming of the factory's power plant, hospitality at Austin and Las Vegas, and driver and engineering access for Bloom's customer events.

ruled_out.reason: Aramco is title partner and Valvoline the lubricants partner; an energy major owns the lane.
Petronas is title partner and the longest-standing energy relationship on the grid.
Mobil 1 and Esso hold fuel and lubricants; Oracle as title partner is Bloom's customer, which makes a power partner look like a supplier placement rather than a brand story.
Mobil 1 on the roster; sister team of Oracle Red Bull Racing.
bp/Castrol joined as fuel and lubricants partner for 2026.
Toyota Gazoo Racing is the technical partner, and Toyota sells its own certified stationary fuel-cell generators; a rival fuel-cell brand on the car is a conflict.

Open but not chosen: an inaugural roster (Core Scientific, TWG AI) on a General Motors-branded team; GM ended its own Hydrotec fuel-cell programme in October 2025, so no live conflict, but a parent that has just exited fuel cells is an awkward host for one.

Schneider Electric joined for 2026 as the energy-management partner, the closest thing to Bloom's category on the grid; the lane is taken. The Groq relationship of Bloom's CFO remains a warm contact, not an opening.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with KR Sridhar before the US GP to confirm the Grove workstream is real for Williams, agree an Austin announcement window, and size an Official Power Partner entry against Williams' 2027 roster.
